notes: Functionally complete, including the quoted `{}` fix with a test for it, but repeats the inline `Val()=="{" && !Quoted()` checks everywhere instead of factoring out a helper.

Covers the same sites as the reference, including the quoted "{}" case, using repeated inline `&& !Quoted()` checks rather than a helper; it misses the address-suffix check, and the formatter tests it adds exercise code that was not changed.
Adds clean quote-aware Dispenser helpers and uses them at every structural brace check, but leaves the `{}` branch unchanged, so a quoted "{}" on a new line still swallows the line break.

Essentially the same as C3 (Dispenser helpers, all main sites fixed, quoted "{}" branch not updated, address suffix missed), with a smaller but adequate set of dispenser, parse, formatter and adapt tests.
Correct core fix with Dispenser helpers and a reasonable doImport guard, but like C1 it doesn't make the `{}` branch quote-aware; tests are solid, and the formatter tests are tangential.

Clean Dispenser helper methods applied at every structural brace site, but the `{}` branch in directive() is left unchanged, so a quoted "{}" starting a new line is still absorbed into the previous segment; tests are strong, including ArgErr and heredoc.

Closely matches the reference using Token methods (including a quote-aware `{}` check), with thorough dispenser, parser, import/{block} and error-case tests; it only misses the HasSuffix address tweak.

Fixes every structural brace check the reference does, including making quoted "{}" fall through to normal handling, via clean unexported Token helpers; it only misses the quoted address-suffix check, and its dispenser, parser and adapt tests are thorough (heredoc, snippets, {block}, error cases).

Recursive approach works, but the `dir != base` check is effectively dead: it always differs because of the leading slash, so Dir is set for nearly every page, contrary to the comment; tests are good and include resources and term layouts.

Recursive slugBase closely mirrors the reference's parent-walk and handles DisablePathToLower, but the `dir != Base()` check may set Dir even when no slug applies (harmless because the path builder normalizes it), and the test covers sections, a bundle resource, a nested section, taxonomy and term.

Recursive prefix-based slug application that closely mirrors the reference, including unnormalized handling and a found-flag so Dir is set only when a slug exists; the test covers the issue example, a nested slug and taxonomy/term.

Recursive slugBaseDir with a found flag only overrides Dir when a slug actually applies, keeping existing behavior otherwise and matching the reference's logic, and the test covers nested section slugs, taxonomy and term, but not bundle resources.
Uses essentially the same segment-index replacement as C1, starting from CurrentSection with a cmp.Or fallback; correct and concise, and the test covers resources, nested sections, taxonomy and term.

Walks the current section and its ancestors and replaces the matching directory segment (by slash count) with each slug; this correctly handles sections, nested sections, leaf bundles, resources, taxonomies and terms, though index-based segment replacement is less self-evident than the recursive approach, and the test covers all the cases listed.

Walks up the branch ancestors and swaps in each slug at the path segment given by that section's path depth; this handles nested non-section dirs, taxonomies and terms, and lets url keep precedence, with strong tests for all of these.

Segment-replacement approach keyed on `p.Path()` slash count works and skips home and standalone pages, and its two tests cover nested slugs, url overrides, page slugs within slugged sections, and terms without content files.

The core fix matches the reference (flat statement list plus first-wins dedup per instance in expandResourceImports), but the extra static dedup in FindImportStatements is redundant and only keys on the resource instance key, so a parent block targeting one module instance could drop a child block for every module instance.

Returns every import statement and adds the same first-wins per-instance check at expansion time as the reference, but it also keeps a static pre-dedup on ConfigResource plus instance key that is redundant and ignores module instance keys, so a parent block targeting module.child["x"] would wrongly drop the child's block for every other module instance.

Fixes the same-module case by grouping statements per ConfigResource, but a parent block still overrides the child at the config-resource level, so child blocks for other instances are silently dropped (the same failure mode in module form); importConfig also stays importTargets[0], and it fails 2/3 hidden tests.

Keeps multiple same-module blocks, which fixes the reported root-module case, but still drops every child-module block for a resource whenever a parent has any block for it, so per-instance precedence across modules is wrong (fails 2/3 hidden tests), and its tests encode that wrong behavior.

Same coarse per-ConfigResource parent override as C1, so per-instance parent/child overlap still drops child imports; the added importConfigForInstance helper is an ad hoc partial fix that ignores module paths, and it fails 2/3 hidden tests.

Uses the same per-ConfigResource grouping as C3, so a parent block still suppresses all child blocks for other instances (fails 2/3 hidden tests); the added importConfigForInstance re-parses addresses in a hacky way, and the tests codify the incorrect override semantics.

Correct per-instance precedence and it also threads the correct import config per instance, with thorough tests, but it adds heavy signature churn, an unneeded transform_config grouping change, and the same redundant static dedup with the module-instance edge bug.

Fixes the bug with per-instance first-wins and, beyond the reference, carries the correct import config per instance instead of importTargets[0]; however it has the same module-instance-blind static pre-dedup as C1, rewrites types across node_resource_plan.go, and adds a transform_config.go regrouping the issue did not need.

Works for the main paths, but it needlessly calls DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts when no scenarios exist, which can raise spurious errors or warnings for shortcuts that --once should simply override; it also ships unrelated proxy-env TestMain workarounds.

Core behavior is correct with thorough unit and integration tests, but it adds unrelated proxy-clearing TestMain hacks in two packages, and it needlessly runs DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts for the no-scenario case.

Minimal, idiomatic rewrite after consolidation with good table-driven unit tests and integration runs, though it shares the gap around lower-layer shortcuts clearing scenarios and does not reject execution-segment flags.

Clean rewrite after consolidation that preserves exec/env/tags/options and rejects CLI shortcut conflicts and multiple scenarios, but it misses lower-layer shortcuts (e.g. K6_ITERATIONS) clearing script scenarios before the merge, and does not reject the execution-segment flags.

The core rewrite is correct and placed right after consolidation like the reference, but it misses two things: env/script-layer shortcuts can wipe the script's scenarios before the rewrite, and execution-segment flags are not rejected; it also adds unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain changes to two test packages.

Well-structured once.go closely mirroring the reference, with sorted scenario names in the error and good tests, but it ships unrelated TestMain proxy workarounds and ignores lower-layer shortcut and execution-segment edge cases.

Clean, focused implementation with a small help-text addition and the strongest tests (consolidation cases, conflict and multi-scenario runs, archive metadata check), though like the others it doesn't pre-drop lower-layer shortcuts that can clear the scenarios during merge.

Correct rewrite before derivation so the archive reflects --once, with the strongest tests (config-consolidation layering cases plus run and archive integration), though, like the others, it misses lower-layer shortcut dropping and the execution-segment conflicts.

Runtime semantics are close to the reference: it always buffers, a bare return returns output so far, and early return works everywhere. But it edits the forked parse.go to rewrite return pipelines, which is exactly the kind of intrusive fork change the issue wants to avoid; it also leaves a vestigial bool return, swallows valued returns in defines, and fails one hidden test.

The runtime design is clean and close to the reference: a ReturnError carrying the value, bare return keeps rendered output, HasReturn removed. However, it edits the forked parse.go directly to rewrite return pipelines, which the issue explicitly warns hurts fork maintainability, it adds docs churn, and values returned inside {{template}} are lost.

Uses an ErrReturn sentinel turned into a returnSignal panic, trapped at template boundaries, with the partial's value carried in a context-scoped PartialReturn; it removes all the wrapper and HasReturn complexity and passes every test. The weak spots are a valued return outside partials being silently ignored, possible context leakage into nested renders, direct edits to exec.go without updating the fork script, and the 13600 test being rewritten so `| string` after return is silently dropped.

This is a working early-return design: an ErrReturn sentinel plus a context-held PartialReturn value, trapped at template boundaries, with return values propagating out of define blocks and try passthrough. It silently ignores value returns in regular templates and non-final pipeline returns where the reference errors, and the context-based value plumbing could leak into nested executions; tests are thorough.

Its ReturnError with HasValue is close to the issue's suggestion. It still uses HasReturn to discard output, so an unexecuted return yields nil instead of the rendered text, and walkTemplate swallows valued returns; tests are a single combined integration test, and one hidden test fails.

The core sentinel approach works: it panics on ReturnError, traps it at template boundaries and lets it pass through try. It keeps the HasReturn/io.Discard hack, so a partial whose value-return branch isn't taken yields nil, and a value returned from a {{template}} is lost. It also weakens the 13600 test to match its own behavior and edits exec.go without updating the fork script.

The panic-based ReturnError is a reasonable core. However, it keeps HasReturn and io.Discard, so a partial whose return branch isn't hit yields nil and its rendered output is lost; it also adds a fragile inSubTemplate flag and drops valued returns inside defined templates, failing two hidden tests.

It always wraps the single return argument in a pipe, so {{ return nil }} breaks with 'nil is not a command'. It retains HasReturn/io.Discard, so untaken value-returns yield nil, and a doc comment is detached from its function. The inSubTemplate tracking is thoughtful and the tests are reasonable.

Closest to the reference, including the Pretty unary-plus fix, and it keeps positive-duration validation; however wrapped nodes take the literal's position rather than the parens', the div/mod check misses negated forms like -(0), and the tests encode odd positions with FIXME comments.

Lifts a parenthesised literal into a wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in both paren contexts, matching the reference, and includes the reference's Pretty fix; it also makes the positive, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero parse-time checks look through the wrapper so they keep firing, with thorough AST, error, printer and calculateDuration tests (minor FIXME notes left in the tests).

Clean unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr approach close to the reference, with paren-accurate positions and a non-mutating unwrap helper that keeps the positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero validations; good parse, printer and evaluation tests, but Pretty is not updated.

Clean wrap helper using the paren token positions plus an unwrap helper that keeps the positive and zero-divisor checks working through the wrapper; tests cover AST, error cases, printer and calculateDuration, but the Pretty unary-plus inconsistency is not addressed.

Works, but it adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and changes its String(), and it still needs a unary-plus DurationExpr wrapper (durationExprOf) in offset, matrix and subquery rules, giving two overlapping mechanisms and more grammar churn; negated forms like foo[-(5)] lose their parse-time check.

Round-trips correctly, but it adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and edits the offset, matrix and subquery rules, so parens are represented in two different ways; AST positions are odd (the literal's range starts at the sign but excludes ')'), and parse-time rejection of `foo[-(5)]` is lost, as in the reference.

Wraps a parenthesised literal in a unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr with accurate paren positions, and extends the positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero checks to see through it, so parse-time validation is kept; it does not update DurationExpr.Pretty, and gating the offset wrap on the experimental flag makes the AST shape depend on that mode.

Same wrap-in-unary-plus approach with paren-accurate positions and a recursive constant check that keeps parse-time positive and zero-divisor validation, with a defensive experimental-flag guard; it skips the Pretty consistency fix and adds no error-case tests for the changed validation.
